title: Commercial Lead
descriptionHtml:
About Griffin

Hi, we’re Griffin. We’re a fully regulated UK bank that powers the accounts and payments offerings of product-led fintechs and platforms like Uber, Yonder, Prosper, and Sidekick. By doing the heavy lifting behind the scenes, our customers can focus on what they do best - delivering amazing customer experiences.

We’ve grown rapidly since our launch in 2024, and today provide the banking backbone behind products in remittance, payroll, wealth, insurance, proptech, payments, neobanking and more.

We’re moving into card issuing, stablecoin infrastructure, and agentic finance next as we continue to support the next generation of product-led companies.

Learn more about what we do

Our culture

We believe that smart, motivated, conscientious people thrive in high-trust, high-autonomy environments and have done our best to create such an environment at Griffin. People who thrive here don’t require much hand-holding, and go out of their way to figure out how to contribute in the most valuable way possible.

We've been remote-first since we were established in 2017 and we remain so today. Work here is asynchronous and fully flexible - because we want to be a part of your life in a way that helps you to get the most out of both your work and home life.

We understand that our culture and ways of working aren’t for everyone, and we’re very intentional about our hiring process as a result. We won't hire people who don’t seem like a strong fit for our core values, even if they're otherwise extremely qualified.

Our strong culture has helped us to remain a mission-driven company as we have scaled, and gives our people a clear, explicit operating framework and the space to focus on delivering real value for our customers.

Learn more about our culture.

The team

We’re the Connect team, what most companies call Sales. We strive to bring the best in technology, user experience and banking to the embedded finance space and be the bank for fintechs and corporates to build on.

We’re 10 people across Commercial, Customers Success and Marketing, led by Phoebe, our Chief Revenue Officer and we’re currently focused on winning new businesses and selecting the right customers to partner with for long term mutual success.

The opportunity

You’ll take Griffin’s licensed bank and banking-as-a-service proposition to mid-market and enterprise companies in payments, lending, proptech, vertical SaaS, insurtech and digital assets. You’ll own each deal from first lead to signed commercial terms. You’ll show their engineering, product, risk and compliance teams how it all works, from API architecture and safeguarding to ledger flows, and talk with confidence to their CFO, COO or CTO. You’ll build your own pipeline, shape pricing for complex accounts with RevOps and Finance, and work with Legal, Compliance and Product on bespoke client needs. Think solutions architect who closes.

What success looks like

Within 12 months, you’ll have built a pipeline you sourced yourself, with deals that are bigger and more structured as you go. Prospects’ CFOs and CTOs will trust you to explain how it all works, and Legal, Compliance and Product will bring you in early on every non-standard deal.

To do this you’ll own

  • Your pipeline, from first lead to signed commercial terms, including sourcing your own leads alongside whatever SDRs and marketing bring in

  • Whiteboard sessions on account structures, and the technical proposal content, which you’ll write yourself

  • Pricing and commercial structures for complex accounts, such as consumption-based or bundled models, tiered volume and transfer pricing, built with RevOps and Finance

  • Regulatory and compliance questions, answered before they turn into objections

  • Commercial and technical arrangements for non-standard client requirements, shaped with Legal, Compliance and Product

Your background

To ensure this, we’re looking for people who have:

  • Built and closed their own pipeline, and get their energy from chasing and winning new business

  • A strong grasp of payments and banking infrastructure (settlement, safeguarding, ledgers, APIs, card and account issuing) and enough regulatory knowledge (EMI versus bank licence, Consumer Duty, safeguarding rules) to hold a credible conversation with a compliance team

  • Sold complex deals with long cycles and several buying committees, and negotiated beyond simple discounting, including pricing models, volume commitments and contractual carve-outs

  • A low ego and high curiosity, with a real appetite for understanding how the plumbing works

  • The resilience for long, technical sales cycles, and the confidence to work without a fixed script while our products and structures evolve

  • A love of writing - we have a major amount of written documentation that you will be contributing to, and we place a high degree of importance on clarity and readability (you can find out more here about how we write)


Nice to haves

Ideally, you would also:

  • Have worked at a BaaS provider, EMI or challenger bank, including in an SMCR-regulated environment

  • Have a structuring background, such as transaction structuring, treasury or Big 4 financial services advisory

What can we offer you?

We are an early stage startup and we're working hard to expand our benefits package. We're planning to add to this list in the future.

  • Salary: Up to £100,000 + commission

  • Remote-first flexibility: Work from anywhere in the UK. However, for this role you will need to be comfortable with regular travel to London, often at short notice.

  • Work from abroad: Up to 20 days a year

  • Time off: 25 days’ holiday, bank holidays and a winter break (we shut down between Christmas and New Year)

  • Share options: Own a part of what we’re building together

  • Pension: Auto-enrolment into our Penfold scheme

  • Insurance: Private medical with Bupa (including family cover) and life insurance with AIG

  • Wellbeing: 1:1 coaching and therapy session available through Oliva

  • Family leave: Enhanced parental leave with up to 6 months on full pay after two years’ service

  • AI tools: Everyone has a Claude subscription on us and access to other premium tools

  • Your setup: We’ll support you in creating a comfortable and effective WFH environment.

How long will the process take?

We move as fast as possible, but it normally takes us about 2-3 weeks to get to know to each other.

  • Step 1: An initial phone call with our Talent Team for us to tell you more about Griffin and learn about your recent experience.

  • Step 2: Meet your manager to talk through your experience and how that relates to the requirements.

  • Step 3: A task based on what you’ll be doing on a day to day at Griffin.

  • Step 4: Meet with peers in your team for a more in-depth technical interview.

  • Step 5: Pitch the Founder and CRevO

  • Step 6: Culture interview: Learn more about this here.

As a bank, we’re committed to maintaining the highest standards of security. This means that the successful candidate will need to complete background screening, and our offer will be conditional upon satisfactory review of these checks. This would include verification of right to work, criminal record, credit history, social media and professional reference checks

How do I apply?

Are we your next move? Apply via the link below, if there's a match our Talent team will reach out to schedule an initial conversation and talk you through what happens next.

Under representation

At Griffin, we’re looking for people who instinctively vibe with our values, behaviours and mission. You’re encouraged to apply, even if your experience doesn’t tick every box. Careers, like life, can take many twists and turns. Your technical expertise and path to where you are today will stand out. We're committed to creating a place where everyone belongs and we welcome diverse perspectives, backgrounds and people who are ready to build a global platform for programmable finance

Griffin Bank Ltd request that recruitment agencies do not speculatively submit CVs to any employee or associate of our company unless explicitly asked to do so by a member of our Talent team.

Any CVs sent to any member of our team on a speculative basis will not be recognised and we will not accept liability for any fee or commission should we subsequently employ a candidate who applied to us directly or was introduced by an instructed agency that may also have been submitted speculatively by an uninstructed agency.

descriptionHtml:
At Axle Energy, we’re building the infrastructure that will underpin the decarbonised energy system. Our software moves energy usage to times when electricity is cheap and green, by controlling vehicle charging, heating systems, and home batteries. We control hundreds of thousands of energy assets.

We’re building in a legacy industry and moving gigawatt-hours of electrons in the real world, but we operate at lightning speed, and we’re growing the team to meet customer demand.

We’re proud to be supported by world-leading investors, including Energize Capital and Accel.

Read more about what we’re building here.

This role is for someone who can drive go-to-market success and build a repeatable commercial motion as Axle grows.

You’ll help customers adopt our technology, commercialise flexibility across their customer base, and expand usage over time. You’ll be expected to move quickly, remove friction, and adapt processes pragmatically rather than getting stuck in bureaucracy.

We’re looking for someone with strong commercial instincts, a sharp GTM mindset, and the ability to operate comfortably in technical conversations.

This role will own

  • Winning new business

  • Developing and managing our growing sales pipeline

  • Go-to-market strategy and execution

  • Client onboarding and ongoing commercial relationship management

What you will be doing

  • Defining sales at Axle, as we establish our go-to-market approach. You will have the ability to make an immediate contribution to our rapidly increasing revenue growth

  • Owning new customer acquisition end-to-end, from first conversation through to commercial close, setting our partners up to generate meaningful revenue (bonus points if you can do this in multiple languages)

  • Driving go-to-market execution with partners, including value propositions, pricing considerations, customer segmentation, and launch strategies

What success looks like

Benefits

A meaningful slice of equity in Axle, alongside a competitive salary, with total compensation ranging from £75k–£200k (base salary + equity).

We operate with a deliberately flat structure and aim to keep pay equitable across the company, with a 1:1 median ratio between founder and team compensation.

Enhanced parental leave to support you through life's meaningful moments.

Bi-annual retreats to strengthen team connection & shared purpose.

Hybrid working - We have a dog-friendly office around Farringdon. To maximize collaboration, we ask that you spend 2-3 days a week in the office.

The opportunity to directly shape the future of energy markets and accelerate the transition to a low-carbon world.

We are extremely keen to build a diverse company, and we’re particularly eager to hear from candidates who don't fit the traditional role stereotypes. If you’re motivated by our mission, please do reach out, even if you feel you might not ‘check all the boxes’.

Interview process

  1. Initial interview

  2. Take-home exercise

  3. Final interview (in-person)

  4. Offer, references, and welcome to the team!

Compensation: £75K – £200K

title: Consumer PR - Business Director
descriptionHtml:
Consumer PR - Business Director

Department: Consumer PR & Influence
Location: London
Contract Type: Fixed-Term 12-Months
Full Time/Part time: Full Time
Reporting into: Managing Partner 

About Ogilvy: 

Ogilvy UK has been creating iconic ideas that deliver impact at scale for clients ever since David Ogilvy founded the company in 1948. The agency specialises in bringing together brand advertising, customer experience marketing, PR, influence and consulting, all fuelled by Behavioural Science. Our world-class award-winning creative campaigns deliver solutions for clients including Sainsbury’s, Lloyds Banking Group, Madri, Unilever and Mondelēz International. 

Ogilvy’s influencer marketing practice is the largest globally; we are proud to be the most awarded influencer agency for eight years running and the recipient of the Cannes Grand Prix for Social & Creator for two consecutive years.   
 
 

The Role: 

As Business Director you will lead client partnership, strategic counsel and integrated delivery across the portfolio, designed to provide the client with fully focused, senior leadership on some of the world’s most iconic FMCG brands. 

The role sits at the intersection of earned-first thinking, culture-led marketing, and integrated agency delivery, ensuring that PR, social, influence and advertising work together to create impact at scale across diverse markets. 
 
This pivotal role places you at the heart of our operations for large FMCG portfolio, one of the world's most iconic and dynamic brands.  

Your remit will span from the initial spark of ideation – identifying trends and innovative opportunities that drive cultural relevance – through the meticulous development of cutting-edge strategies tailored to diverse market nuances and brand objectives. You will lead the charge on defining compelling creative narratives and content frameworks, ensuring brand consistency and breakthrough engagement. Subsequently, you will oversee flawless execution, transforming strategy into impactful activations across various platforms and geographies.  

This role demands a holistic leader capable of driving innovation, navigating complex client relationships, and delivering measurable results within a dynamic, multi-market agency environment. 
 

Key Responsibilities: 

Client leadership & stakeholder management 

  • Act as the senior day-to-day client lead for European and Global teams, building trusted, long-term partnerships
  • Provide strategic counsel across brand, reputation, partnerships and cultural activation
  • Lead complex, multi-market stakeholder management across global, regional and local teams
  • Ensure the FMCG Brand has consistent, senior-level leadership fully embedded in the brand business 

Global & European strategy development 

  • Lead the creation of global and European communications toolkits, frameworks and playbooks that balance global brand consistency with local market nuance
  • Embed earned-first thinking into all toolkits
  • Partner closely with creative and strategy leads to shape culturally relevant, insight-led ideas 

Market management & intelligence 

  • Oversee market engagement across Europe and priority global territories, acting as a central connector between the brands global teams and local markets
  • Ensure clients are consistently informed on market trends, cultural shifts, competitor activity and emerging opportunities
  • Champion local market insight, ensuring work is adaptable, relevant and executable across diverse regions 

Global events & partnerships 

  • Lead the communications strategy and delivery for global brand moments and events, ensuring alignment across markets
  • Play a central role in developing and activating brand partnerships, embedding them seamlessly into toolkits and campaign narratives
  • Work with market and agency leads to bring partnerships to life in locally relevant, culturally resonant ways 

Team leadership & integration 

  • Directly manage a London-based team, working alongside creative and strategy leadership
  • Foster a collaborative, high-performance team culture grounded in integration and shared ownership 

What makes this role different: 

  • 100% dedicated to the FMCG portfolio, allowing for deep brand immersion and long-term strategic thinking
  • Operates at true global scale, balancing global brand stewardship with local market realities
  • Deeply partnership-led, with collaborations embedded into brand strategy
  • Strong emphasis on earned-first, culture-first marketing, influencing how integrated campaigns are built from the ground up
  • Sits within a fully integrated agency model, requiring constant collaboration across discipline 

Key Leadership Competencies: 

  • Proven experience in global and/or European leadership roles, ideally within FMCG or large-scale consumer brands 
  • Exceptional stakeholder management skills — this role is heavily relationship-driven and requires confidence navigating complexity 
  • Strong understanding of how global brands operate across markets, with sensitivity to cultural and market nuance 
  • Demonstrated experience working in integrated agency environments across PR, advertising, social and influence 
  • A passion for culture-led, earned-first marketing and its role in driving brand relevance and business impact 
  • Commercially astute, strategically minded and comfortable operating at senior client level 
  • A genuine interest in — and affinity for — the drinks brands and the wider FMCG landscape 
  • Communication & Collaboration: Defines and communicates the overarching vision for the Influence practice. Develops communication strategies that align the department with agency leadership and fosters a culture of open dialogue and mentorship for senior leaders. 
  • Organisation & Resource Management: Architects the department's operational structure to support profitability and growth. Oversees P&L, leads resource forecasting, and ensures the practice is structured to handle complex, large-scale business needs. 
  • Responsibility & Accountability: Holds ultimate accountability for the entire department's commercial and creative performance. Empowers directors to lead their teams while maintaining transparent, high-level communication with executive leadership on business progress and challenges. 
  • Problem Solving & Decision Making: Acts as the final point of authority on the most critical business issues. Makes high-stakes decisions that protect the agency's commercial interests and mentors directors in strategic problem-solving. 
  • Growth & Development: Champions and funds a departmental learning culture. Defines the long-term talent strategy, creates career pathways for all levels, and builds a best-in-class team through senior hiring and mentorship. 
  • Ogilvy Values & Behaviours: Acts as the ultimate custodian of the agency's values within the department. Embeds these values into the practice's core processes, from recruitment and client management to performance recognition. 
      

Skills for Your Growth to Client Partner: 
To support your progression, you will be expected to develop capabilities in the following areas: 

  • C-Suite Partnership & Business Acumen: Transition from a practice leader to a C-suite strategic advisor. Develop a deep, holistic understanding of the client's entire business model, competitive landscape, and financial drivers to become an indispensable partner to their most senior leaders. 
  • Integrated Solution Leadership: Evolve from leading a single capability to orchestrating the agency's full suite of services. Master the art of integrating diverse crafts—from brand advertising and PR to consulting and data—to solve the client's most complex business problems. 
  • Enterprise Commercial Strategy: Shift focus from departmental P&L management to owning the entire client commercial relationship. Drive enterprise-level growth by identifying strategic opportunities across the client's organization and negotiating large-scale, multi-year partnerships. 
  • Relationship as the Core Product: Move from a role where the craft is the primary product to one where the strategic client relationship itself is the core deliverable. Your success will be measured by your ability to build unwavering trust and long-term loyalty at the highest levels. 
     

Personal Qualities: 

  • Extensive and proven experience in a senior leadership role (e.g., Senior Account Director or Business Director) within a top-tier agency.
  • Strategic yet pragmatic
  • Culturally curious and globally minded
  • Confident, collaborative and calm under pressure
  • Energised by complexity, scale and partnership-driven work
  • Demonstrated track record of P&L ownership and delivering significant, year-on-year business growth.
  • Proven success in leading and winning multi-million-pound new business pitches.
  • Exceptional leadership skills with experience in shaping departmental culture and developing senior talent.
  • Strategic visionary with the ability to anticipate market trends and define a clear, forward-looking path for the business.

How we help you Thrive:

title: Content Lead
descriptionHtml:
Content Lead

Reporting to: CMO

Location: London (hybrid, 4 days a week in the office)

Salary: £80,000-£100,000 + equity

About Electric Twin

Most organisations make their biggest decisions on a thin slice of evidence - a handful of customer calls, one survey, instinct when the data runs out. Electric Twin changes that. We build synthetic audiences: simulations of real groups of people, grounded in research data. Teams ask them questions, test ideas and explore how people might respond, and get answers in minutes that would otherwise take weeks.

The work is grounded, and the science is real. We've run over 40,000 evaluations across populations covering 155 countries. Independent academic research with Professor Michael Muthukrishna at the LSE found our outputs come back roughly 10,000x faster than traditional methods, at 95% accuracy. Customers including The Times, Sage, Virgin, Vodafone and Wingstop use Electric Twin to bring customer insight into decisions about campaigns, products, pricing and strategy.

Electric Twin was founded by Dr Ben Warner (former Chief Data Advisor to the UK Prime Minister) and our CEO, Alex Cooper (a former senior military commander and Director of Mass Covid Testing in the pandemic). We're backed by Atomico, LocalGlobe, Mercuri and angels including Marc Andreessen. We're a team of engineers, AI researchers, behavioural scientists and operators - careful with the science, careful with the responsibility.

The role

We're hiring our first Content Lead to own content at Electric Twin, from the strategy through to what goes out each week.

Our ambition is to make understanding people a normal part of making decisions. Content is central to that: helping people understand a new category, showing what's possible and giving them evidence they can trust.

There's a lot to work with: research, founder perspectives, customer evidence, existing content, and scientists and customers with interesting stories to tell. What's missing is one person who sets the direction and runs the operation day to day.

You'll work closely with our CMO and our product marketer. Our Head of Growth runs the engine - the channels and programmes that reach and convert our audience. Product marketing and content provide the fuel. Product marketing owns positioning and messaging. You’ll take it, turn it into compelling stories and get them out across every channel.

This is a hands-on role. You'll set the strategy and direct agencies and freelancers, and you'll also spend a meaningful part of your week writing and editing.

What you'll do

Strategy

  • Own our content strategy. Take our positioning, messaging pillars and core messages, and decide what we turn them into, where each piece goes and how it lines up with our SEO, AI and PR work.

  • Shape the category narrative. Synthetic audiences are new to most of our buyers. Help them understand the category, see what's possible and find evidence they can trust.

  • Plan content across the buying journey. Earn attention at the top of the funnel, then build out the mid-funnel, where we have the biggest gap today, with content that helps people evaluate us. Know what each piece is for and what it should help someone do next.

Writing and publishing

  • Write and edit. Founder LinkedIn posts, articles, website copy, reports, campaign content and nurture emails. Make complex ideas clear and relevant to the people we want to reach.

  • Develop our founders' voices. Work with our founders, Ben and Alex, to turn their experience and perspectives into distinctive content, particularly on LinkedIn.

  • Repurpose and distribute. Take research, customer stories, product launches and product marketing insight, and adapt them for each channel. Work with growth to get them in front of the right people.

  • Run the editorial plan. Own the publishing calendar across LinkedIn, the blog and email, so everyone knows what’s going out and when.

Building the function

  • Build the content operation. Briefs, editorial standards, production workflows, approvals and a reliable publishing rhythm. Use AI to build repeatable systems for researching, creating, adapting and distributing content, while keeping it accurate, original and high quality.

  • Direct external support. Brief and manage our agency partners and freelancers, set clear priorities and hold their work to a high standard.

  • Partner with performance. Work closely with growth, bringing a good understanding of how content drives growth. Track how it contributes to reach, engagement, organic discovery and pipeline, and use that to decide what we make next.

Your first six months

  • Set our content strategy - building on our positioning, messaging pillars and the content we already have.

  • Take full ownership of the editorial plan, with a consistent publishing rhythm across LinkedIn, the blog and email.

  • Fill the mid-funnel, so buyers evaluating Electric Twin have the content they need to move forward.

  • Make Ben and Alex distinctive voices on LinkedIn, with a regular cadence of posts that sound like them.

  • Launch nurture email beyond product comms.

  • Get the content operation running, with clear briefs, editorial standards, AI workflows, and agency partners and freelancers producing work to a high standard.

What we're looking for

Experience

  • You've owned content strategy and delivery at a B2B technology company, and can show how your work helped build its reputation and commercial growth.

  • You've built or substantially improved a content operation in a fast-moving company where processes and priorities were still taking shape.

  • You've worked with founders or senior leaders, capturing their thinking and developing a voice that sounds like them.

  • You've owned channels end to end, from the idea through to publishing, learning and iterating. You've created content for awareness, consideration and evaluation, and you understand SEO, search intent and what works natively on each channel.

  • You've partnered with product marketing and growth, and briefed and managed agencies and freelancers. You have a network of freelancers and agencies you can call on to scale our content.

Skills and approach

  • An excellent writer and editor. You find the interesting angle, interview experts well and turn complicated subjects into clear, engaging content.

  • Comfortable with strategy and execution. You can produce a high-level plan on your own, then write the first piece yourself.

  • You've used AI to build repeatable content workflows, and you can judge when the output is good enough and when it isn't.

  • Careful with the details. You're comfortable getting to grips with AI, research and technical subjects, you ask good questions and you check claims carefully.

  • You take ownership and think ahead. You spot what needs doing, make a recommendation and see it through, and you give people time to contribute.

  • You're happy taking feedback and you make getting things done easy.

  • Experience producing video content for social channels including YouTube and TikTok.

What we offer

  • £80,000-£90,000 base

  • Meaningful equity in a high-potential seed-stage company

  • Unlimited leave. Take the time you need

  • Generous matched pension contributions

  • Private healthcare

  • Cycle to work scheme

  • Founding content hire with real influence over how the function is built

  • Direct access to and collaboration with world-class founders

  • Hybrid working from our London office (4 days in office a week)

  • Flexible working around life commitments. We value outcomes over presenteeism

When you apply, please share examples of your writing and a content strategy or operation you've built, explaining your contribution and what it achieved.

descriptionHtml:

About the Role:

This role reports to the Site Lead. The Senior Manager, Maintenance leads the maintenance and reliability function for a GMP peptide manufacturing facility, providing high-level support to the Site Operations and Engineering organization through predictive and preventive maintenance programs for all production, utility, and facility equipment. This position analyzes, troubleshoots, and communicates maintenance problems and concerns in the following areas: electrical, mechanical, plumbing, compressed air and process gases, HVAC, and clean utilities, as they relate to equipment and controlled environments in the facility. The Senior Manager works with general supervision and will interact with the Site Lead regularly to receive guidance and feedback. Many non-routine activities will require the Site Lead’s advance approval.

You Will:

  • Lead a group of maintenance technicians, supervisors, and managers across a multi-shift, multi-discipline operation.

  • Own the predictive and preventive maintenance program for all GMP equipment, including peptide synthesizers, preparative HPLC and purification systems, lyophilizers, filtration and TFF skids, reactors, isolators and hoods, autoclaves, and associated controls.

  • Maintain and reliably operate facility and clean utilities, including HVAC and cleanroom environmental systems, purified water/WFI, clean steam, compressed air, nitrogen and other process gases, and chilled and hot water systems.

  • Document maintenance, technical, and other data on predictive/preventive maintenance charts, as required.

  • Diagnose and repair equipment and systems throughout the facility, including electrical, mechanical, plumbing, compressed air, PLC/controls, and HVAC repairs.

  • Identify facility and equipment issues and develop an ongoing strategy to chart trends and take remedial action using a predictive maintenance approach.

  • Communicate to management all issues that could result in safety risks, product quality impact, or loss to Hims or its associates.

  • Work as directed in all areas of the facility to maintain safety and health standards.

  • Perform and oversee calibration and testing procedures on equipment to ensure accurate operation and compliance with quality standards.

  • Conduct regular checks and measurements to verify equipment performance, including temperature, pressure, speed, and other relevant parameters.

  • Maintain calibration records and documentation in compliance with cGMP and other regulatory requirements.

  • Ensure that all equipment meets regulatory and quality standards and take corrective actions to address any non-compliance issues.

  • Collaborate with Quality Assurance, Validation, and Regulatory Affairs to implement and maintain proper documentation, including equipment logs, maintenance records, change controls, deviations/CAPAs, and qualification and validation reports.

  • Support equipment and facility qualification (IQ/OQ/PQ), commissioning, and requalification activities, and maintain the validated state of equipment through the change control process.

  • Respond promptly to equipment breakdowns, emergencies, and production interruptions to minimize downtime.

  • Work closely with production personnel to coordinate repairs and planned maintenance and minimize disruptions to the manufacturing schedule.

  • Develop and manage the maintenance budget, spare parts strategy, and external contractor and vendor relationships.

  • Identify opportunities for process optimization, efficiency improvements, and cost savings related to equipment maintenance and operation.

  • Participate in cross-functional teams to implement improvement projects and contribute to a continuous improvement culture within the organization.

  • Stay updated with industry trends, technological advancements, and best practices related to pharmaceutical and peptide manufacturing equipment maintenance.

  • Make sure all assets, parts, and work orders are updated and tracked in CMMS for all facility equipment.

You Have:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Maintenance, or a related technical field; equivalent technical training/certification may be considered.

  • 5+ years of maintenance or engineering experience in pharmaceutical manufacturing or another highly regulated environment.

  • 10+ years of people leadership experience, including leading hourly and salaried technical teams.

  • Strong working knowledge of cGMP requirements and maintaining equipment in a GMP environment.

  • Hands-on expertise troubleshooting and maintaining advanced mechanical, electrical, and automated equipment, including PLC and CMMS systems.

  • Experience leading preventive and predictive maintenance programs, interpreting technical data, and driving equipment reliability and continuous-improvement initiatives.

  • Demonstrated ability to lead, develop, and assess technical talent; delegate complex work; and build effective shift and staffing structures.

  • Experience partnering across multiple facilities or teams to implement scalable maintenance systems and solve network-level operational challenges.

  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to present recommendations to senior leaders.

  • Ability to meet the physical requirements of the role, including lifting up to 50 pounds, working at heights, climbing ladders/stairs, and operating safely in an industrial environment.

  • Availability to support urgent operational needs outside regular business hours.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience in pharmaceutical, API, peptide, or other GMP manufacturing environments.

  • Technical certification or formal training in electrical, mechanical, HVAC, plumbing, compressed air, or PLC systems.

  • Advanced degree or training in engineering, maintenance, Lean, Six Sigma, or a related discipline.

  • Spanish language skills.

Renewals are the core of a SaaS company's revenue. You own renewal targets for Samsara's Digital Mid-Market segment: setting customers up for success while maximising financial results. On every deal that means minimising attrition, locking in the best terms, spotting growth opportunities, feeding insights back to the business and closing 36-month renewals.

You should apply if:

  • You want to impact the industries that run our world: Your efforts will result in real-world impact—helping to keep the lights on, get food into grocery stores, and most importantly, ensure workers return home safely.
  • You have an innate curiosity about how businesses work: One day you'll meet with someone in waste management and the next you may be learning about the inner workings of a food distribution center. Our top sales team members seek to learn the ins and outs of the businesses they support in order to make a larger impact.
  • You enjoy working at high velocity:
  • You want to be with the best: Samsara's high-performance culture means you'll be surrounded by the best and challenged to go farther than you have before.
  • You are a team player: At Samsara, sales is a team sport. We help each other out by sharing best practices and focusing on winning as a team.

In this role, you will:

  • Own 60+ renewals per quarter from end-to-end and exceed sales targets
  • Follow a structured scenario-based forecasting methodology
  • Engage with customers to identify and mitigate renewal risk and drive platform adoption at scale
  • Work cross-functionally with sales teams to solve problems and ensure a successful, smooth renewal
  • Contribute to an exceptional team environment that motivates the team to perform at its best
  • Champion, role model, and embed Samsara's cultural principles (Focus on Customer Success, Build for the Long Term, Adopt a Growth Mindset, Be Inclusive, Win as a Team) as we scale globally and across new offices

Minimum requirements for the role:

  • Business fluency in French (spoken and written).
  • 2+ years of full-cycle closing sales experience, ideally with mid-sized businesses in a high-transaction environment.
  • A record of consistent quota over-achievement.
  • Comfort in a fast-changing, high-growth environment.
  • Empathy for customers and teammates, and strong organisation.
  • Strong communication and presentation skills.
  • Familiarity with Salesforce.

Total Rewards

At Samsara, we build for the people who keep the global economy moving. We want owners, not passengers, which is why our rewards are designed to fuel high-impact builders. Our compensation program delivers above-market total compensation through a combination of base salary, performance-based bonus/variable pay, and equity (for eligible roles) in a high-growth public company. We meaningfully differentiate pay for our top performers, who have the opportunity to earn above-market compensation that can outpace the broader market over time.

Beyond compensation, we provide the foundations that enable long-term success: a flexible, employee-led remote model, a professional development stipend, comprehensive health and parental leave plans, and more. If you're ready to build for the long term and own the outcome, your journey starts here.

Flexible Working

At Samsara, we embrace a flexible working model that caters to the diverse needs of our teams. Our offices are open for those who prefer to work in-person and we also support remote work where it aligns with our operational requirements. For certain positions, being close to one of our offices or within a specific geographic area is important to facilitate collaboration, access to resources, or alignment with our service regions. In these cases, the job description will clearly indicate any working location requirements. Our goal is to ensure that all members of our team can contribute effectively, whether they are working on-site, in a hybrid model, or fully remotely. All offers of employment are contingent upon an individual's ability to secure and maintain the legal right to work at the company and in the specified work location, if applicable.

Belonging at Samsara

At Samsara, we welcome everyone regardless of their background. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, sex, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, protected veteran status, disability, age, and other characteristics protected by law. We depend on the unique approaches of our team members to help us solve complex problems and want to ensure that Samsara is a place where people from all backgrounds can make an impact.

Accommodations

Samsara is an inclusive work environment, and we are committed to ensuring equal opportunity in employment for qualified persons with disabilities. Please email click here if you require any reasonable accommodations throughout the recruiting process.

Our Commitment to Authenticity

We use Tofu, a fraud detection tool, to validate the authenticity of applications and protect against identity fraud. This ensures we are connecting with real people and allows us to prioritize genuine candidates. Please see Samsara's Candidate Privacy Notice for more information.

title: Customer Success Manager II
descriptionHtml:
About Pleo

Messy spend management is tricky business. And tedious processes are a lose-lose situation for all involved, not just finance. At Pleo, we're changing that. We build spend solutions that make managing money seamless, empowering, and surprisingly effective for finance teams and employees alike - with a vision to help all businesses ‘go beyond’.

The word ‘Pleo’ actually means ‘more than you’d expect’, and living by that mantra has been the secret to our success over the last 10 years.

Now, we’re at a pivotal moment in our journey; every move we make has a direct impact on our 40,000+ customers, our business, and our collective success. We need people who take pride in uncovering customer needs, who turn complex problems into simple solutions, challenge the way things are done (respectfully), and always aim high. With great ambitions driving us forward, we can’t say we’ve got this whole thing figured out. And frankly, that’s half the fun! What we can say is that we’re a driven, progressive, and, importantly, a kind bunch of 850+ people from over 100 nationalities, all committed to delivering the future of business spending, together.

About the role

We're looking for a Customer Success Manager II to join our Customer Experience team at Pleo. In this role, you'll help our SMB and Mid Market customers achieve success and maximise the value of Pleo’s solutions and be part of a dynamic and collaborative team as we scale our innovative expense management platform across the UK & Ireland

If you're excited about solving customer challenges, and driving growth through exceptional service and are passionate about Customer Success in the SaaS industry, then this is the opportunity for you!

 

Who you’ll be working with and reporting to

You’ll report to our CX Manager and work closely with teams in CX, Onboarding, AM, Sales and Product. Our team of 30 is highly collaborative and dedicated to Customer Experience.

 

What you’ll be doing

As a Customer Success Manager II, your main markets will be UKI customers. You will:

  • Nurture, support and process expansion for any opportunity from the customer base

  • As a customer's trusted product advisor and business consultant advise them on how to create their ideal processes with the tool to optimise their value-add

  • Own the adoption journey of your customer portfolio (after the onboarding phase)

  • Collaborate across teams with different internal stakeholders such as product management, services & solutions, marketing, customer support, etc. to improve the entire customer experience

  • Receive, qualify and triage all inbound communication from all communication channels; email, Intercom (web chat), and/or other performance marketing channels

  • Cultivate key customers to become advocates of Pleo and the Fintech community

  • Manage day-to-day operations and long-term business relationships with our customers

  • Do everything in your power to prevent customers from leaving Pleo through measuring health scores, and product/ feature adoption and acting proactively on those

  • Optimise the product-market-fit by building the bridge between the customer's feedback and our product team

 

What you bring


You’ll thrive in this role if:

  • You have 5+ years of prior experience in account management or sales or customer success roles

  • You have an open mindset that always looks for the positive. Your customers and colleagues find your energy contagious

  • You truly enjoy helping others move and improve. You love helping your customers scale and grow

  • You love goals and objectives. You don't always need to be given tasks – you create your own tasks while chasing your targets, and it motivates you to reach them

  • You love a fast-paced and dynamic environment, where you have different kinds of tasks - from customer calls to meetings with our product team

  • This is a high volume, high velocity role. Being able to think and do things at scale is a huge plus

  • You are a trustworthy person who always ensures that deadlines are reached, promises are kept, and you do what is expected of you

  • You are empathetic. You have a strong ability to feel how others are doing. You are also able to communicate in a very empathetic way and touch people's emotions

  • You are fluent in English

     

Why is this role a good fit for you

 

This role is a good fit for you if:

  • You enjoy building long-term relationships with SMB and Mid Market customers and taking ownership of their success from adoption through expansion.

  • You thrive in a fast-paced, high-volume environment and feel energised by balancing customer conversations, internal collaboration, and proactive problem-solving.

  • You’re motivated by impact and outcomes — helping customers grow, spotting expansion opportunities, and turning feedback into meaningful product improvements excites you.

This role is not a good fit for you if:

  • You’re not motivated by customer-facing work or influencing customer outcomes through proactive engagement and collaboration.

  • You’re uncomfortable with project management or coordinating multiple initiatives at the same time.

  • You’re not motivated by upselling, cross-selling, or optimising the long-term value of your customers’ accounts.

     

How you’ll develop in this role

In your first 6 months at Pleo, you’ll:

  • Lead customer adoption projects to drive impact in helping SMB and Mid Market clients maximise the value of Pleo’s solutions.

  • Collaborate with Customer Success and Product teams to improve customer experience processes and feedback loops.

  • Grow your skills in relationship management and upselling strategies, taking on new challenges as the company continues to scale.

We’re committed to helping you develop your career, whether that means taking on bigger projects, stepping into leadership, or acquiring new skills in customer success.

 

The location

Lisbon, Portugal, or London, UK

 

Show me the benefits!

  • Your own Pleo card (no more out-of-pocket spending!)

  • Lunch is on us for your work days - enjoy catered meals or receive a lunch allowance based on your local office

  • Comprehensive private healthcare - depending on your location, coverage options include Vitality, Alan or Médis

  • We offer 25 days of holiday + your public holidays

  • For our Team, we offer both hybrid and fully remote working options

  • Option to purchase 5 additional days of holiday through a salary sacrifice

  • We use MyndUp to give our employees access to free mental health and well-being support with great success so far

  • Paid parental leave - we want to make sure that we're supportive of families and help you feel that you don't have to compromise your family due to work


The interview process

We want to ensure you are set-up for success and understand what will be expected of you. If your application is successful, our interview process is as follows:

  1. Intro call: A 30-minute chat with our Talent Partner to discuss the role and your background.

  2. A 30-45 minute call with the Hiring Manager

  3. Our Pleo Challenge - an opportunity for you to showcase your ability in the form of a presentation and how you would approach the task at hand

  4. Final Interview - Our Bar Raiser meeting - how would you raise the bar for us?

Transparency is important to us so we also wanted to share some insights about what we’re looking for in applications to ensure you can set yourself up for success!

Last time we hired a CSM, we received many applications but only a few were selected for an intro call. Some of the key reasons why previous candidates didn’t make it past the application screening stage include:

  • CV writing and content: we receive a lot of CVs, and many of them are AI-generated. We love seeing people leverage AI—it’s a big focus for us internally too—but without human intervention, these CVs can sometimes become generic and fail to show a candidate in the best light. What we're really looking for is the specific details of real impact that only you know from your previous experience. A top tip from us is to use the “Achieved X, as measured by Y, by doing Z” formula (credit: Laszlo Bock, ~2014) to give a really clear picture of what you’ve worked on. A final note: including links to your previous companies' websites is a huge help and allows us to truly understand your background!

  • Application care: every single application we receive is reviewed by a human (yes, hundreds of them) because we believe that candidates' efforts should be matched by an equal level of human care. This means that we expect a similar level of attention put into your application. Read and answer the application questions carefully, they make a huge difference in our decision-making process.

  • Profile to role fit: highlight most important aspects of the role, points that might get misunderstood, any specific industry requirements etc.

About your application

  • English first. Since it's our company language, please submit your application in English. You’ll be using it a lot if you join us.

  • A fair look for everyone. Our talent team reads every single application to ensure the process is fair. To keep things running smoothly, we only accept applications through our system—our support team can’t pass on calls or emails.

  • Diversity drives us. We can only reach our goals if our team reflects the world around us. That starts with you hitting apply, even if you don't tick every single box. We encourage people from all backgrounds and experiences to join us.

  • Interview at your best. We want you to feel comfortable throughout the process. If you have any accessibility requirements or need a specific format, email ----- We’ll design a process that works for you.

  • Your data is safe. When you apply, we process your personal data as a data processor. For more information on how Pleo processes personal data, read our Privacy Policy here.

  • Applying for multiple roles? Nothing is stopping you, and we assess every role independently. However, we do look for alignment, so make sure you can explain why your interest and experience are right for each specific role.

  • Reapplying. If you’re applying for the same role again, please wait six months from your last decision before hitting submit.

title: Customer Success Team Lead (German-speaking)
descriptionHtml:

At Secfix, we're at the forefront of automating security compliance in Europe. We help companies get and stay ISO 27001, GDPR, TISAX, and SOC 2 fast and easy and reduce hundreds of hours of manual work.

Secfix is run by a 100% remote team with the exception of our DACH sales team, which is based in Munich. We're a high-performing team looking for passionate, execution-focused, owners to help us automate security and compliance for modern companies and become the European compliance automation leader.

We've raised our $12M Series A and are backed by top VCs, including Alstin Capital, Neosfer (Commerzbank), and Bayern Capital.

This is where careers are made!

About the Role

Our CSM team has grown to five Customer Success Managers, each running a book of customers through ISO 27001, SOC 2, TISAX, NIS 2 and DORA. As the team keeps growing, we're creating a dedicated Team Lead role: a manager who works alongside the CSMs every day and makes their coaching and development a priority!

Lead the CSM team

  • Line-manage the CSMs: regular 1:1s, structured feedback, input to performance reviews and individual development plans

  • Own onboarding for new CSMs so they're productive on their first accounts fast

  • Allocate books and manage capacity across the team as customers and CSMs are added

  • Run a team health review covering at risk accounts, renewals and onboarding blockers

  • Own customer escalations within the CSM books

  • Own the CSM playbook and keep it current

  • Decide which CSM workflows to automate, and build the agents and automations with AI

Drive the team's upsell performance

  • Coach CSMs on spotting and running framework and service upsells within their books

Run your own portfolio

About You

You'll be the line manager for all CSMs and run 1:1s, feedback loops, onboarding, and provide inputs to performance reviews and career development, while keeping a reduced portfolio of your own customers (because we don't think you can coach CSMs well on work you don't do).

  • You've managed or formally coached CSMs before for at least 1 year and want to keep doing it; this isn't a first step into management

  • 4+ years as a Customer Success Manager in B2B SaaS, ideally with mid-market or DACH Mittelstand customers

  • Fluent German and English as our CSM team works with customers in both

  • Comfortable with a revenue component: you've carried an upsell or NRR target yourself and can coach others toward one

  • Structured and direct in feedback; you can run a hard performance conversation without the Head of CS in the room

  • You work well in a written-first remote team: clear specs and updates over meetings, high ownership, low need for synchronous oversight

Nice to have

  • Experience in compliance, information security or GRC (ISO 27001 or TISAX in particular)

  • You've built or reworked a CSM onboarding programme before

  • You've worked in a fully remote team of a similar size

Interview Process

  1. Screening call with Steve, our recruiter

  2. Interview with Kuba, Head of Customer Success

  3. Take-home challenge

  4. Challenge interview with Kuba and Fabiola, our CEO

  5. Culture interview with Grigory, CTO

  6. Meet for a final lunch in-person with Kuba (we'll fly you!)

What we offer

  • Competitive Salary: Industry-competitive local salaries. We pay local rates that are at or above the market. We share this philosophy with GitLab.

  • Equity: Generous equity package – we're all owners of Secfix and beneficiaries of our collective success.

title: Data Analyst
descriptionHtml:
Help launch our new temping product and drive commercial impact!

At YoungOnes, data is at the start of every decision. Our Data & RevOps team has a seat at every table and takes a leading role in where the company goes next. Two years ago we rebuilt our data environment in Databricks from scratch, and it is fully ready for the future. There are few better environments to work in.

We are looking for a Data Analyst with a focus on product, who also supports our marketing and commercial teams with deeper analyses. Someone with experience who is ready to take responsibility, and who does not stop at a report but actively steers on the outcome.

What will you do?

Your main focus is product. Next to that, you support marketing and the commercial teams, which keeps your work varied.

Product

In the flexible work market, companies used to choose between temping (uitzenden) and freelancers. Since last year we have been bringing a new proposition to market that sits in between: non-service temping. It combines the legal certainty of temping with the flexibility and personal control of freelancing, all through our platform. This is an important step in our strategy towards one app for work.

  • Take the lead in tracking the progress of this new proposition;

  • Define the KPIs and funnel that show whether the proposition is working;

  • Analyse the full journey of workers and clients, from onboarding to repeat shifts;

  • Spot problems early and actively steer where you see them;

  • Translate insights into concrete improvements together with product and development;

  • Work in a select team that operates as a startup within the company.

Commercial & marketing support

Next to product, you are the analytical sparring partner for our commercial teams and marketing. You go beyond the standard reports and dive deeper when questions get complex.

  • Deliver deeper analyses for the commercial teams, for example on client potential, retention and growth opportunities;

  • Support marketing with insight into campaign results and ROAS.

This role is diverse, but above all it gives you a lot of freedom to take initiative and make an impact.

Your team

You will join an effective Data & RevOps team with 3 Analysts, 2 Engineers, a Performance Manager and 2 Process aAnalysts. You report to the Head of Data.

The data itself is interesting: we support a two sided marketplace with workers on one side and clients on the other. AI is built into the design of how we work and makes the technical side of your job more simple. We use Genie within Databricks, which fully understands our data environment, Claude to connect multiple systems, and Gemini for quick support on smaller tasks.

What are we looking for?

We are looking for someone who:

  • Has at least 3 years of experience as a Data Analyst, Product Analyst or Commercial Analyst;

  • Has experience tracking and steering product performance, and/or with commercial or marketing analytics;

  • Is strong in SQL and familiar with Python/PySpark and a visualisation tool such as Power BI or Amplitude;

  • Has experience with Databricks, or is eager to work in it;

  • Uses AI tooling naturally to work faster and smarter;

  • Takes ownership and dares to make choices and influence stakeholders;

  • Communicates clearly with both technical and non technical colleagues;

  • Is already residing in the Netherlands and is allowed to work in the country and speaks fluent English (Dutch is a plus);

We are not looking for someone who only delivers reports. We want someone who takes the lead, sees problems before others do and makes sure something is done about them.

What do we offer?

  • A gross salary between €4,300 and €6,100 based on full-time employment;

  • 25 vacation days, 6.5 ADV days and 1 additional holiday per calendar year, based on a 40-hour workweek;

  • 8% vacation pay, a pension plan, and (if you live more than 10 km from the office) a travel allowance;

  • We prioritize mental well-being in collaboration with our partner OpenUp;

  • Great perks such as: a yearly fitness budget, a freshly prepared healthy lunch every day, snacks, biweekly afternoon drinks, XL borrels every three months, sport tournaments, and much more;

  • A leading role in a new proposition that is key to our strategy;

  • One of the best data environments to work in, with Databricks and AI built in;

  • A company that is truly data driven, where your insights shape decisions;

  • A high level of autonomy, freedom and responsibility.

YoungOnes is a place where you learn fast, build fast and see results fast. Ready to take the lead? Then we would love to hear from you.

title: Data, Automatisation & IA – Investissement à impact
descriptionHtml:
L’investissement à impact est un secteur d’activité en forte croissance. INCO Ventures, acteur clé de ce domaine en France, gère et conseille six fonds d’investissement dédiés au financement des entreprises à fort impact social et/ou environnemental. Il investit principalement dans des cibles en changement d’échelle et/ou en développement (tickets d’investissement compris entre 300k€ et 2M€).

Pourquoi nous recrutons

Nous sommes une société de gestion spécialisée dans l’investissement à impact. Nous accompagnons des entreprises qui contribuent aux grandes transitions environnementales et sociales, tout en recherchant une performance financière attractive pour nos investisseurs.

Au fil des années, nous avons construit nos outils et nos processus autour d’Airtable, de différentes solutions SaaS et d’usages ponctuels de l’intelligence artificielle. Cette organisation nous a permis de grandir rapidement.

Aujourd’hui, nous souhaitons franchir une nouvelle étape.

Notre ambition est de construire une véritable plateforme data et IA au service de l’ensemble de notre écosystème :

  • L’équipe de gestion

  • Les équipes middle office et conformité

  • Nos investisseurs (LPs)

  • Les entreprises de notre portefeuille

Concrètement, nous souhaitons faire évoluer notre architecture de données, automatiser davantage nos processus, déployer des usages IA à forte valeur ajoutée et créer des espaces digitaux permettant à chacun d’accéder simplement aux informations dont il ou elle a besoin.

Pour nous accompagner dans cette transformation, nous recrutons un.e stagiaire qui travaillera directement avec le Responsable Conformité & Middle Office ainsi qu’un.e Directeur.rice d’investissement.

Ce stage est autant un projet de construction qu’un projet d’innovation : nous recherchons une personne capable de comprendre les enjeux métier, de proposer des solutions et de contribuer à leur mise en œuvre.

Ce que vous construirez concrètement

Pendant votre stage, vous contribuerez à :

  • Structurer et faire évoluer plusieurs années de données d’investissement, impact et ESG

  • Participer à la migration de notre socle de données vers une architecture moderne et évolutive

  • Déployer des automatisations permettant de réduire les tâches manuelles et d’améliorer la qualité des données

  • Concevoir les premiers assistants IA internes de la société

  • Créer des outils utilisés quotidiennement par les équipes d’investissement, le middle office et la conformité

  • Participer à la création de portails dédiés aux investisseurs et aux entreprises du portefeuille

  • Contribuer à définir notre feuille de route data & IA pour les années à venir

Vos missions

Les projets seront menés en lien direct avec les équipes d'investissement, d’impact, le middle office et la conformité. Vous travaillerez dans un environnement très transversal, avec une forte autonomie et la possibilité de contribuer aussi bien à la réflexion qu'à l'implémentation des solutions.

Les missions décrites ci-dessous constituent une feuille de route initiale. Elles évolueront naturellement en fonction de l’avancement du projet, de vos centres d’intérêt et des opportunités identifiées ensemble.

  1. Comprendre et structurer notre écosystème de données

Vous participerez notamment à :

  • Cartographier les bases Airtable existantes et leurs usages

  • Comprendre les flux de données entre les différentes équipes

  • Identifier les redondances, points de friction et opportunités d’amélioration

  • Participer à la conception du modèle de données cible

  • Contribuer, le cas échéant, à la migration progressive vers Supabase

  • Structurer les données financières, impact et ESG

  • Définir les règles d’accès et de gouvernance des données

  • Documenter les modèles, processus et bonnes pratiques

L’objectif est de construire un socle de données fiable, partagé et durable.

2. Automatiser les processus clés

Une fois les données structurées, vous contribuerez à automatiser les tâches répétitives et à fluidifier les opérations.

Exemples :

  • Collecte de données auprès des participations, relances automatiques

  • Consolidation de reportings

  • Contrôles de cohérence

  • Gestion documentaire

  • Préparation de certains livrables réglementaires

  • Qualification et enrichissement automatique d'opportunités d'investissement

  • Circulation de l’information entre les outils

Vous participerez à la conception et au déploiement de workflows no-code et low-code, principalement via N8N et les APIs des différents outils utilisés par la société.

3. Déployer des usages IA concrets

Nous cherchons quelqu’un qui saura identifier où l’IA peut réellement créer de la valeur.

Vous pourrez notamment travailler sur :

  • Des assistants internes connectés à nos bases de données

  • Des outils de recherche documentaire et de gestion des connaissances

  • L'extraction automatique d'informations depuis des rapports, questionnaires ou documents de due diligence

  • La pré-analyse de dossiers d'investissement

  • La génération assistée de reportings, mémos d’investissement et comptes-rendus

  • Des workflows mêlant automatisation et IA

  • L’exploration de nouveaux cas d’usage liés à l’investissement, à l’impact ou à la conformité

Vous serez encouragé.e à expérimenter, comparer les solutions disponibles sur le marché et proposer vos propres idées.

4. Construire les interfaces et portails utilisateurs

À mesure que les fondations seront en place, vous participerez à la création des interfaces permettant aux différents utilisateurs d’accéder simplement à l’information. Cela pourra inclure :

Portail équipe de gestion

  • Suivi des participations

  • Reporting portefeuille

  • Outils internes de pilotage

Portail investisseurs (LPs)

  • Consultation des reportings

  • Suivi des indicateurs de portefeuille

  • Diffusion sécurisée des informations réglementaires

Portail participations

  • Collecte de données

  • Suivi des indicateurs financiers et extra-financiers

  • Partage documentaire

5. Accompagner l’adoption des nouveaux outils

La réussite du projet ne dépend pas uniquement de la technologie. Vous contribuerez également à :

  • Comprendre les besoins des utilisateurs

  • Identifier de nouveaux cas d’usage

  • Former les équipes aux outils déployés

  • Produire une documentation simple et utile

  • Diffuser les bonnes pratiques liées à la data et à l’IA

  • Réaliser une veille active sur les nouveaux outils et tendances du marché

Pourquoi ce stage est différent

Vous ne rejoindrez pas une équipe technique isolée mais travaillerez directement avec les équipes métiers :

  • Notre Responsable Conformité & Middle Office

  • Notre Chief Impact Officer

  • Nos Directeur.rices d’investissement

Vous serez exposé.e à des problématiques à la fois stratégiques, opérationnelles et technologiques.

Vous participerez à la transformation d’une société de gestion de l’intérieur, avec une forte autonomie et un impact visible dès les premières semaines.

Les outils et processus que vous contribuerez à construire seront utilisés au quotidien par les équipes, les investisseurs et les entreprises que nous accompagnons.

C’est une opportunité rare de développer une expertise à l’intersection de l’investissement, de la data, de l’automatisation et de l’intelligence artificielle.

Candidature

Envoyez-nous votre CV accompagné de quelques lignes expliquant :

  • Ce qui vous attire dans ce projet

  • Un outil, une automatisation ou un usage IA que vous avez déjà mis en place (ou que vous aimeriez explorer)

Pas besoin de lettre de motivation formelle.

Nous privilégions les personnes curieuses, pragmatiques et motivées à construire.


Nous recherchons avant tout une personne curieuse, autonome et orientée solutions.

Vous pourriez être la bonne personne si :

  • Vous êtes en école d’ingénieur, école de commerce, université ou équivalent

  • Vous avez une forte appétence pour la data, l’automatisation et l’IA

  • Vous aimez expérimenter de nouveaux outils

  • Vous êtes capable de transformer un problème métier en solution concrète

  • Vous savez avancer de manière autonome tout en travaillant en équipe

Des compétences ou expériences dans les domaines suivants seront appréciées :

  • SQL et bases de données relationnelles

  • Airtable, Notion, N8N, Make ou outils similaires

  • APIs et intégrations

  • IA générative et prompting

Mais nous accordons autant d’importance à la curiosité, à la capacité d’apprentissage et à l’esprit d’initiative qu’aux compétences techniques.

title: Data Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Bouwen is pas de helft van het werk

Data draait nooit om de tool, maar om de vraag erachter. Als Data Engineer bij LINKIT ga je die vraag niet uit de weg, je zoekt hem juist op.

De uitdaging

Als Data Engineer werk je aan dataplatformen die er in de praktijk toe doen: bij NS aan data-oplossingen voor internationale treinreizen, bij Robeco aan moderne beleggingsplatformen, en bij EDSN en Stedin aan schaalbare data-ecosystemen in de energiesector. Je bouwt en onderhoudt data pipelines in de Cloud, ontwikkelt datatransformaties en datamodellen met SQL en Python, en werkt met tools als Snowflake, Databricks of Fabric en orchestration tools zoals Airflow, dbt of ADF. Je komt in dienst bij LINKIT en gaat aan het werk bij toonaangevende opdrachtgevers in mobiliteit, energie en financiële dienstverlening.

Je hebt een goede basis als Data Engineer en bent klaar voor de volgende stap: niet alleen bouwen, maar ook doorgronden waarom een platform zo is ingericht als het is. Je denkt mee met analytics-, BI- en data-science teams, en ziet feedback als brandstof voor groei.

Je plek: de Data Engineering squad

Je maakt onderdeel uit van de Data Engineering squad: vakinhoudelijke collega's die net als jij nieuwsgierig zijn naar het waarom achter elke oplossing. Kennis delen zit in het DNA van de squad, niet alleen tijdens projecten, maar ook op de clubdag, de tweewekelijkse vrijdag op ons hoofdkantoor in De Meern waarop we tijd vrijmaken voor leren en verbinden. Benieuwd wie je toekomstige collega's zijn?

Lees hier meer over de Data squad.


Wat we vragen

  • Kennis van of ervaring met distributed dataprocessing frameworks/datalakes zoals Spark, Flink, Delta Lake, Iceberg, etc.

  • Ervaring met een cloudplatform zoals Azure, AWS of GCP.

  • Leergierig, open voor feedback en gericht op inhoudelijke/technische groei.

Voldoe je niet aan elk punt, maar wel nieuwsgierig? Dan komen we alsnog graag met je in contact.

Zo verloopt jouw reis naar LINKIT

We willen je leren kennen, en jij ons. Daarom houden we het persoonlijk en concreet.

  1. Kennismaking: Een eerste gesprek over wie je bent, wat je drijft en of er een match is.

Wil je alvast meer weten? Neem gerust contact op met Tabea via

Over LINKIT

LINKIT is opgericht in 1998 en gegroeid van IT-bemiddelaar naar kennisgedreven IT-organisatie, met ruim 250 Explorers uit meer dan 25 nationaliteiten. We werken voor grote organisaties in overheid, finance en logistiek als partner die meedenkt van vraagstuk tot oplossing. Als Data Engineer ga je aan het werk bij toonaangevende opdrachtgevers, met een contract bij LINKIT. Je bepaalt je eigen richting, met een ongelimiteerd opleidingsbudget en de ruimte om te groeien op een manier die bij jou past.

title: Data Engineer (Detect & Track Distillation)
descriptionHtml:
About Us

Harmattan AI is a next-generation defense prime building autonomous and scalable defense systems. Following the close of a $200M Series B, valuing the company at $1.4 billion, we are expanding our teams and capabilities to deliver mission-critical systems to allied forces.

Our work is guided by clear values: building technologies with real-world impact, pursuing excellence in everything we do, setting ambitious goals, and taking on the hardest technical challenges. We operate in a demanding environment where rigor, ownership, and execution are expected.

ABOUT THE ROLE

Our ML teams train models on datasets derived from large volumes of raw, unstructured data. Model quality depends directly on data quality, and today that data is handled largely by hand.

As a Data Engineer, operating out of Paris, Lausanne, or Zurich, you will own the data layer that feeds the team's models, from raw field logs or public datasets through curated, versioned, training-ready datasets. You will manage terabytes of raw, unstructured data and turn it into clean, documented, versioned datasets, so that the modelers spend their time designing and training models, not waiting on data loaders or wrangling corrupted files. You join at an early stage with real influence over how field and public data gets processed for deep-learning pipelines.

RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Ingestion Pipeline: Ingest, decode, and store raw, unstructured field data (video and other sensor streams) from field logs into efficient, controlled formats.

  • Multimodal Alignment: Align multiple data streams temporally and spatially so paired data is usable for training.

  • Curation: Transfer both ingested data and public datasets into high-value data, including parsing, filtering, de-duplication and revision.

  • Data & Labeling Requirements: Define which data to gather and what and how to label it, and own the dataset-construction workflow and labeling tooling. Coordinate with the teams responsible for data gathering and labeling.

  • Dataset Construction: Build task-specific datasets for the team’s training and evaluation needs, in collaboration with acquisition, annotation and product teams.

  • Versioning & Lineage: Version datasets and maintain lineage so training runs stay reproducible.

  • Storage & Formats: Store data in efficient, training-ready formats (such as columnar or sharded formats) and manage storage tiering to balance cost and latency as datasets grow.

  • Efficient Delivery: Deliver clean, documented datasets and the corresponding tools for loading to keep training from being I/O-bound, shaping their structure with the modelers.

CANDIDATE REQUIREMENTS

  • Educational Background: A degree in a STEM field, or equivalent practical experience. Practical data engineering experience matters more than the specific degree.

  • Data Pipelines at Scale: Built and maintained pipelines for unstructured data at scale (video, images, or sensor data), covering ingestion, decode, storage, curation, and versioning.

  • Engineering: Strong in Python and data engineering, and comfortable optimizing data loaders for common training frameworks (for example PyTorch).

  • Bonus: Multimodal sensor data, labeling or dataset construction for ML, dataset versioning tooling, and distributed data processing tooling.

  • Attributes: Systematic, quality-minded, pragmatic, and service-oriented so the modelers are enabled, with a knack for taming messy data via automation.

  • Commitment: 100% dedication to Harmattan AI's mission of providing a defensive edge to allied nations through ethical, high-impact technology.

We look forward to hearing how you can help shape the future of autonomous defense systems at Harmattan AI.

⭐ About Data at Monzo

Data is at the heart of how we make decisions and build products at Monzo. Our Data teams bring together Data Science, Analytics Engineering, Data Analytics and Machine Learning, working closely with Product, Engineering and other teams across the business.

Our Data Scientists are embedded within product and business areas across Monzo, where they use experimentation, causal inference, statistical modelling, machine learning and analytics to understand our customers, identify opportunities and influence the direction of our products and strategy.

We have a strong culture of data-driven decision making across Monzo. We're big believers in powerful, accessible analytics and empowering teams across the business to answer questions themselves. Around 90% of our day-to-day data-driven decisions are supported by self-serve analytics through Looker, giving our Data teams the space to focus on higher-impact problems.

descriptionHtml:
Nous recherchons un-e Data Steward Corporate Operations People basé-e à Lille ou Paris

DECATHLON accélère la transformation et la digitalisation de ses processus RH, en partie grâce à une forte maîtrise de ses données People et de leurs usages. Pour accompagner cette transformation, nous déployons une plateforme RH mondiale intégrant un CORE RH (Workday) et plusieurs modules de talent management (Performance, Comp&Ben, Career management...).

Au cœur de la réussite de Decathlon se trouve notre engagement envers nos 100 000 collaborateurs. L’équipe People Data joue un rôle essentiel dans ce développement. En rejoignant notre équipe pluridisciplinaire (plus de 30 experts : Data Product Managers, Data Analysts, BI engineers, Analytics Engineers, Data Engineers et d’experts en Gouvernance de données), vous travaillerez sur l'ensemble des processus RH et serez le garant de la gestion et de la protection de nos données.

Vos responsabilités principales

En tant que Data Steward, vous jouerez un rôle essentiel dans la gestion et la protection des données au sein de l'entreprise. Vous travaillerez en étroite collaboration avec les équipes métiers, les équipes IT et les autres parties prenantes pour garantir que les données de votre domaine soient documentées, fiables, accessibles et conformes aux normes internes et réglementaires :

  • Documentation & discoverability : vous participez à la structuration des concepts business et garantissez une documentation cohérente et centralisée dans le Data Catalog (Collibra). Vous assurez le lineage entre les concepts métiers et les connaissances techniques
  • Accessibilité de la donnée : vous traduisez les besoins métiers en exigences techniques d'exposition, et accompagnez les Data Users dans la localisation et l'utilisation des données en favorisant l'usage du Data Catalog. Vous vous assurez que les ingestions de données dans le Datalake respectent les standards (storage zone, schémas, nomenclatures…)
  • Sécurité & conformité : vous veillez à ce que la donnée reste strictement conforme aux exigences de sécurité et aux règles légales (ex: CNIL, RGPD, PIPL). Vous vérifiez l'alignement avec le registre de traitement du DPO
  • Animation & collaboration : vous collaborez activement avec les Data Owners, Data Quality Manager, Data Manager, Product Owners/Data Producers et équipes techniques (Data Engineers, BI Engineers). Vous contribuez également à la communauté globale des Data Stewards pour améliorer la maturité et faire évoluer les standards.

Votre écosystème & les spécificités RH

  • Outils & processus : vous évoluerez dans un écosystème marqué par des solutions telles que Workday, des outils d'acquisition de talents (ex: GreenHouse), et des systèmes de paie locaux et globaux.
  • Objets de données : vous documenterez des entités propres aux ressources humaines (Job profile, Worker, Payroll, Cost Center, etc.).
  • Enjeu clé de conformité : une attention extrême sera portée à la confidentialité des données personnelles et sensibles des collaborateurs.

Ce dont vous aurez besoin pour réussir

  • Expérience : solide background en Data Stewardship, idéalement sur des projets RH, dans un environnement complexe et multi-pays
  • Savoir-faire technique : maîtrise de l'usage d'un Data Catalog (idéalement Collibra), compréhension des écosystèmes Data (API, Datalake, Data Warehouse), requêtes SQL simples, et méthodologies Agiles (Jira). Connaissance des environnements Cloud (Databricks, Tableau)
  • Savoir-être : rigueur, excellent esprit d'analyse et de synthèse, sens du service. Capacité à convaincre, à vulgariser et à fédérer des interlocuteurs variés. Anglais courant indispensable (niveau B2/C1) pour collaborer avec le réseau mondial.
  • Niveau d'autonomie : capacité à travailler en autonomie sur des périmètres complexes, à influencer les bonnes pratiques et à animer des initiatives transverses à fort impact.

Ce que nous t’offrons

  • Mode de travail hybride (3 jours sur site / 2 jours de télétravail)

  • Développement des compétences et accompagnement (diversité des projets, certifications techniques dès la première année, formations internes et externes, etc.)

NOTRE ENGAGEMENT EN FAVEUR DE L'INCLUSION ET DE L'ACCESSIBILITE

Chez Decathlon, nous reconnaissons l'immense valeur qu'apporte la diversité à nos équipes et nous nous efforçons continuellement de favoriser et de cultiver un lieu de travail inclusif et équitable : c'est pourquoi l'Inclusion est l'un de nos Fondamentaux Humains.
